title: The best PhoneBurner alternatives in 2026
summary: PhoneBurner alternatives for 2026, ranked. Artisan runs calling inside one AI outbound system, plus Nooks, Orum, Salesfinity and more.
body_markdown:
The best PhoneBurner alternative for most teams is[Artisan](https://www.artisan.co/) , because it puts calling inside one AI-run outbound system instead of a standalone single-line power dialer. PhoneBurner is a well-built single-line dialer. If you want parallel volume or the whole motion run by AI, an all-in-one wins.


PhoneBurner is deliberately single-line: one call at a time, no connect delay, with its ARMOR system working to keep numbers off spam lists. This design produces clean, human-feeling calls, and it is the tool's point of pride. It does not parallel dial, though, and it does not source leads, write and send email, or handle replies. Teams shopping for an alternative usually want either more connects per hour or the whole outbound job run by AI.

## How we chose


We weighted the criteria for a buyer who is deciding whether single-line power dialing is enough or they need more.


1. How much of the outbound job the tool does. A dialer improves connect rates, while a full system connects calling to sourcing, email, and reply-handling.


2. Connect volume per hour. Single-line pacing versus parallel dialing with AI answer detection, and what that does to conversations per rep.


3. Number reputation and compliance. Spam remediation, per-number ceilings, and automatic enforcement of calling hours, do-not-contact (DNC) rules, and consent-aware recording.


4. Pricing transparency and deployment fit. Published pricing, pooled numbers, callback routing, and CRM owner mapping at scale.


## Why do teams look for a PhoneBurner alternative?


Two reasons dominate. PhoneBurner is single-line by design, and it only covers calling.


The single-line choice is deliberate and defensible. One call at a time with no dead air produces natural conversations and protects caller ID, which is why relationship-led sellers like it. It also caps connects per hour. A team that is trying to raise the number of live conversations per rep runs into the ceiling of one line, and starts looking at[parallel dialers](https://www.artisan.co/blog/best-autodialers) that place several calls at once with AI answer detection. This is a genuine step-change in volume that single-line pacing cannot match.


The second limit is scope. PhoneBurner dials, logs, and protects numbers with ARMOR, and this is the boundary. It does not find best-fit leads, write and send personalized email sequences, or qualify and answer replies. So a real outbound motion pairs PhoneBurner with a data provider, a sequencer, and a deliverability layer, then reconciles the reporting. The dialer is solid, and the stack around it is the cost.


The triggers we hear:


-


You need more connects per hour. One line at a time limits how many live conversations a rep can start.


-


Calling is only part of the job. Sourcing, email, and reply-handling still live in other tools.


-


You want spam protection inside a broader system. ARMOR guards numbers, but only for the calling you run in PhoneBurner.


None of this makes PhoneBurner a bad dialer. It makes it the wrong center of gravity for a team that wants parallel volume or the whole motion run by AI.


## The best PhoneBurner alternatives in 2026


### 1. Artisan: Calling inside one AI-run outbound system


Artisan is the alternative for teams that want the dialer to be a step in a larger, AI-run motion instead of a standalone single-line tool. Calls run as steps inside Ava's multichannel sequences alongside email and social media, so the same system that sources the lead and writes the message also places the call and logs the outcome. Ava parallel dials up to three lines with AI answer detection, loads live AI talking points before the call connects, transcribes live, auto-classifies outcomes, drafts the follow-up email, and can drop a voicemail with automatic area-code matching. Your rep handles the live conversation.


On the number-reputation worry that PhoneBurner's ARMOR targets, Artisan protects connect rates at the org level: carrier spam-reputation monitoring, per-number call ceilings, and automatic area-code matching, with numbers pooled across the org and personal callback routing so a lead calling back reaches the right rep's phone. Calling-hours enforcement, federal DNC checks, and consent-aware recording apply automatically per lead. Central admin maps CRM owners so calls log to the right rep. Numbers cover the US, UK, and Canada.


The economics work differently from a per-seat dialer. Artisan prices on usage, so cost tracks the work performed rather than the number of reps who might dial this month, and the dialer seat includes unlimited minutes along with the talking points, transcription, AI-drafted follow-ups, recordings, and analytics. Because the wider outbound motion also lives here, you replace the data tool, sequencer, and deliverability layer at the same time.


The honest concession is line count. Artisan parallel dials up to 3 lines. Nooks and Orum reach 5 to 10. A team whose entire motion is maximum-volume parallel calling, nothing else, may still want a dedicated floor. For everyone whose calling sits inside a broader outbound motion, one system beats a single-line dialer plus a stack.


SaaStr saw the difference in output. Amelia Lerutte, Chief AI Officer at SaaStr, put it plainly: "Email has always been our number one driver. Artisan is now neck-and-neck in both output and closed-won revenue." In roughly six weeks, Ava sent 6,892 emails at a 3.6% positive response rate, alongside a 49.4% social media connection acceptance rate.


**Best for:** startups through enterprise that want calling as one channel in an AI-run outbound system.


**Who should pick something else:** pure call floors whose only job is maximum-volume parallel dialing at 5 to 10 lines.


**Pricing:** usage-based. See[artisan.co/pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### 2. Nooks: High-volume parallel call floor


[Nooks](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-nooks) is the alternative for the exact problem PhoneBurner's single line creates, which is too few connects per hour. It parallel dials across multiple lines with AI answer detection and runs a virtual salesfloor with live coaching, which multiplies live conversations for high-volume calling teams. If your reason for leaving is line count, Nooks is a category leader.


The trade is scope and price. Nooks is calling-only, so sourcing, email, and replies live elsewhere, and[its pricing is demo-gated](https://www.artisan.co/blog/nooks-pricing-and-reviews) , reportedly around $4,000 to $5,000/user/year on annual terms. Our[dialer roundup](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-ai-dialers-and-parallel-dialers) breaks down the pure-parallel options.


**Best for:** teams moving from single-line power dialing to a high-volume parallel salesfloor.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want calling connected to the rest of outbound, or published pricing.


**Pricing:** demo-gated; reportedly around $4,000 to $5,000/user/year, annual.


### 3. Orum: Enterprise parallel with global reach


[Orum](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-orum) suits large teams whose motion really is high-volume parallel calling across borders. It parallel dials 5 to 10 lines with AI answer detection, offers international dialing on its Ascend tier, and acquired the conversation-intelligence tool Scout AI in July 2026. For a dedicated call floor at enterprise scale, Orum is a leader.


Like Nooks, it is calling-only and its pricing is gated, reported near $250/user/month. The sourcing, email, and reply-handling live in other tools, so it solves the connect-volume problem but not the stack problem.


**Best for:** enterprise call floors that need 5 to 10 lines and broad international coverage.


**Pricing:** roughly $250/user/month reported, gated.


### 4. Salesfinity: Transparent parallel pricing


Salesfinity is the pick for teams that want the connect-volume jump from single-line to parallel without a demo to see the price. It publishes $149 to $349/user/month for five lines, which makes it the transparent alternative in the pure-dialer tier. For a calling team that values knowing the cost up front, that openness is a real advantage.


Salesfinity is still a dedicated dialer, so it dials and the rest of your outbound stack sits elsewhere. Among standalone parallel dialers, its pricing transparency stands out.


**Best for:** calling teams that want 5-line parallel dialing at a published price.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want the dialer inside a full outbound system.


**Pricing:** $149 to $349/user/month for 5 lines, per Salesfinity's pricing page.


### 5. Koncert: Multiple dialing modes


Koncert suits teams that want flexibility in how they dial. It offers several modes, an AI parallel dialer, a flow dialer, and an agent-assisted dialer, so reps can match the dialing style to the campaign, including a parallel option PhoneBurner does not offer. This range makes it adaptable across calling motions in one tool.


Koncert is a dedicated dialing platform, so it handles the call and not the surrounding motion. It publishes per-tier pricing, which helps buyers compare without a sales call.


**Best for:** teams that want to switch between parallel, flow, and agent-assisted dialing.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that want calling unified with sourcing, email, and replies.


**Pricing:** published per-tier pricing, per Koncert's pricing page.


### 6. Kixie: Dialer plus texting for SMB


[Kixie](https://www.artisan.co/blog/kixie-vs-justcall-which-should-you-choose-in-2026) is the alternative for smaller teams that want a power dialer bundled with SMS and tight CRM logging. Like PhoneBurner it leans on power dialing rather than high-volume parallel, but it adds texting to the mix, which suits small and medium-sized business (SMB) teams that want calls and texts in one place. Its published per-seat pricing keeps it accessible.


Kixie is not a high-volume parallel floor, so teams that chase connect-rate multipliers will still look elsewhere. It fits SMB motions rather than enterprise call floors.


**Best for:** SMB teams that want calling, texting, and CRM logging in one tool.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need high-line parallel dialing or an AI-run full motion.


**Pricing:** published per-seat pricing, per Kixie's pricing page.


### 7. JustCall: Calls, SMS, and automations


JustCall is the alternative for SMB and mid-market teams that want a cloud phone with calling, texting, and workflow automations in one place. It suits teams that want their telephony and messaging unified with CRM integrations, a different mix from PhoneBurner's calling focus.


It is more communications platform than high-volume parallel floor, so teams that chase connect multipliers or a full AI-run motion will look elsewhere. Its per-seat pricing is published.


**Best for:** SMB teams that want calls, texting, and automations in one communications tool.


**Who should pick something else:** teams that need parallel dialing or an AI-run full outbound motion.


**Pricing:** published per-seat pricing, per JustCall's pricing page.


## Stay with PhoneBurner if...


PhoneBurner is the right call for a specific profile. Keep it if:


-


Your selling is relationship-led and call quality matters more than raw connect volume, so single-line pacing with no dead air is a feature rather than a limit.


-


Number reputation is your top concern and ARMOR's spam remediation is doing the job for the calling you run.


-


You already run a settled stack for sourcing, email, and replies, and you only need a clean single-line dialer to plug into it.


Switching away from a deliberately single-line tool to chase parallel volume you do not need is a mistake. If your motion values conversation quality over connect count, PhoneBurner is a defensible place to stay. If you need more connects per hour or want the whole motion run by AI, this is the signal to move.


## How a single-line power dialer compares to an AI BDR


The decision hinges on whether calling is your whole motion or one channel in it. A single-line dialer like PhoneBurner maximizes call quality on the phone, and does nothing else. An[AI sales agent](https://www.artisan.co/ai-sales-agent) like Ava dials calls as one step in a sequence that also sources the lead, writes and sends the email, and handles the reply, all in one system, with spam-reputation monitoring built in.


If your team only calls and values single-line quality, PhoneBurner covers it. If your team runs multichannel outbound, buying a standalone dialer means buying and stitching a stack around it. Consolidating into an AI business development representative (BDR) removes the stitching and adds parallel lines without giving up reputation protection. See the[AI BDR explainer](https://www.artisan.co/blog/ai-bdr) for how the role works.


## What changed in dialers in 2026?


-


Orum acquired the conversation-intelligence tool Scout AI in July 2026, deepening its post-call analytics.


-


Spam flagging and number reputation stayed the category's number-one buyer worry, which is exactly what PhoneBurner's ARMOR and Artisan's reputation monitoring both target.


-


Usage-based dialer economics gained ground against demo-gated pricing as buyers pushed back on quote-only models.


-


Parallel dialing kept moving from a standalone category toward a channel inside broader AI-run outbound systems.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best alternative to PhoneBurner?


For teams that want calling connected to the rest of outbound, Artisan is the strongest alternative, because the dialer runs inside Ava's multichannel sequences with spam-reputation monitoring built in. For teams that mainly want more connects per hour, Nooks or Orum add high-volume parallel dialing at 5 to 10 lines.


### What is the best enterprise alternative to PhoneBurner?


Artisan, for teams that want calling governed inside one system: pooled org-level numbers, callback routing, automatic DNC and calling-hours enforcement, CRM owner mapping, and per-number ceilings, on usage-based pricing that stays predictable as the team grows. Orum is the enterprise pick if the motion is purely maximum-volume parallel calling across many countries.


### Does PhoneBurner do parallel dialing?


No. PhoneBurner is deliberately single-line, one call at a time with no connect delay, paired with ARMOR spam remediation. Teams that want several simultaneous lines move to a parallel dialer like Nooks, Orum, Salesfinity, or Koncert, or to Artisan, which parallel dials up to 3 lines inside a full outbound system.


### How much does PhoneBurner cost?


PhoneBurner publishes per-seat pricing on its site, with plans from roughly $140 to $183/user/month on annual billing. Artisan prices on usage instead, so you pay for the work performed rather than a fixed seat count, and the same platform adds sourcing, email, and reply-handling. See[artisan.co/pricing](https://www.artisan.co/pricing) .


### How does Artisan protect number reputation like ARMOR does?


Artisan monitors carrier spam reputation, enforces per-number call ceilings, matches area codes automatically, and pools numbers at the org level with callback routing. Those protections run across the calling inside Ava's sequences, alongside automatic DNC checks, calling-hours enforcement, and consent-aware recording.


### How many parallel lines does Artisan support?


Artisan parallel dials up to 3 lines with AI answer detection, a step up from PhoneBurner's single line. Nooks and Orum reach 5 to 10 lines. For a team whose whole motion is maximum-volume calling, that higher line count matters. For teams where calling is one channel in a broader sequence, 3 lines inside one system is usually the better trade.
